_comment: The whole P2D2 cell from Rendering/p2d2.urdf -- rail, both carriages, both MOATs, the m710ic50 arms and their hands: 34 links and 33 joints, drawn as ONE articulated object.
_it_is_already_flat: p2d2.urdf contains no xacro at all (it is a plain <robot> with concrete link and joint names), so unlike Hand/Hand.urdf.xacro there is nothing to instantiate or flatten -- it imports directly.
_it_draws_its_own_rail: rail_link sits at this URDF's root with an identity origin and carries Rail\visual\Rail.stl. So loading this object puts a rail on screen whether or not rail.json draws one -- which is why rail.json keeps visible:false. Two copies of the same 10 m mesh at the same place is not a second opinion, it is z-fighting.

placements._comment: Where the cell's root sits. Identity, because p2d2.urdf's rail_link IS the rail datum that rail_origin names -- the two frames are the same frame by construction, so no offset is owed.

The articulated cell. Posed by forward kinematics from the controller's joint state when the robot bridge exists; until then it holds the URDF's home pose, which is what the 'NO JOINT STATE' banner is reporting.
placements._ONE_ARTICULATED_ROBOT_AT_A_TIME: RobotScene keeps a SINGLE robot description (robot_, jointIndex_, articulatedId_ and the root transform are all one each, not per-placement), and importArticulated overwrites them. With both this object and 'hand' loaded, the LAST joint_state placement imported wins that slot and is the only one that gets re-posed or carried to its mount; the other one's link rows keep the world poses they were given at load. Both are at their home pose here so both still draw correctly -- but do not read this scene as proof that two live articulated objects work, because they do not yet.
placements._topic: The CONTROLLER's joint state, not the cameras'. Nothing publishes it yet, which is a roadmap item rather than a fault.
